exact_steps: FieldForce Pro is a web-based Field Service Management (FSM) platform. It centralises work orders, scheduling, dispatch, customer management, invoicing, and reporting for field service businesses (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, cleaning, security, landscaping, etc.).

The application is divided into two areas:
**Sidebar (left):** Primary navigation. Sections include:
- Dashboard / Home
- Service Requests
- Work Orders
- Scheduling
- Contacts (customers and companies)
- Service Locations
- Assets
- Invoices
- Estimates
- Timesheets
- Reports
- Settings
- Admin (super-admin only)
**Top bar:** User profile, notifications bell, theme toggle (light/dark), and the AI assistant (Max) chat button.

| Role | Primary Access |
|------|----------------|
| **Admin** | Full access — all modules, settings, user management |
| **Dispatcher** | Service requests, work orders, scheduling, contacts |
| **Technician** | Assigned work orders (read/update), timesheets, mobile app |
| **Manager** | Reports, approvals, read-only across all modules |
Roles and their exact permissions are configurable in **Settings → Roles & Permissions**.

Every entity follows a defined status lifecycle. Status transitions are validated server-side — you cannot skip steps.
`New` → `Estimated` → `Approved` → `Scheduled` → `In Progress` → `On Hold` → `Completed` → `Closed` → `Cancelled`
`New` → `Triaged` → `Estimated` → `Approved` → `Converted to WO` → `Closed` → `Spam`
`Draft` → `Sent` → `Viewed` → `Approved` → `Rejected` → `Expired` → `Converted to WO`
`Draft` → `Sent` → `Viewed` → `Partially Paid` → `Paid` → `Overdue` → `Void`
`Scheduled` → `Dispatched` → `In Transit` → `On Site` → `In Progress` → `On Hold` → `Completed` → `Cancelled`
Each organisation (tenant) is fully isolated. Users can only see data belonging to their own tenant. Tenant settings are managed under **Settings → Organisation**.

Most list pages (Work Orders, Contacts, Invoices, etc.) support:

Work orders are the core operational unit of FieldForce Pro. They represent a job to be performed at a customer's location.

- **Customer / Contact** — link to an existing contact
- **Service Location** — the address where the job takes place
3. Optional: attach an **Asset**, set a **Scheduled Start** date, or assign a **Technician**.
4. Click **Save**. The work order is created in `New` status.

| **Notes** | Internal notes and communication log |
| **Attachments** | Photos, documents, PDFs |
| **Job Sheet** | Digital checklist for the technician |
| **Appointments** | Linked service appointments |
| **Invoice** | Invoice generated from this work order |
| **Activity** | Audit trail of all status changes |

1. Go to **Settings → Roles & Permissions**.

1. Go to **Settings → Organisation**.

2. Update:
- **Company Name** — shown on invoices and customer emails
- **Logo** — upload a PNG/JPG (recommended: 200×60px, white or transparent background)
- **Default Timezone** — affects all scheduling and reports
- **Default Currency** — used in invoices; can be overridden per invoice
- **Date Format** — DD/MM/YYYY or MM/DD/YYYY
3. Click **Save**.
SLAs define how quickly you must respond to and resolve jobs.
1. Go to **Settings → SLA Policies**.
2. Click **+ New Policy**.

3. Fill in:
- **Policy Name**
- **Priority** — which work order priority this applies to (Low / Medium / High / Urgent)
- **First Response Time** — e.g., 2 hours
- **Resolution Time** — e.g., 8 hours
- **Business Hours** — whether the clock runs 24/7 or only during business hours
4. Click **Save**.
5. Assign the policy to a customer or a default in Organisation Settings.
Workflow rules automatically perform an action when a trigger condition is met.
1. Go to **Settings → Workflow Rules**.
2. Click **+ New Rule**.

3. Configure:
- **Trigger** — e.g., `Work Order status changes to Completed`
- **Conditions** (optional) — e.g., `Priority is Urgent`
- **Action** — e.g., `Send email to customer`, `Create follow-up task`, `Webhook POST`

4. Click **Save and Activate**.
### Example Rules
- When a work order is `Completed`, automatically create an invoice draft.
- When a service request is `New` for more than 2 hours, escalate priority to `High`.
- When an invoice becomes `Overdue`, send a reminder email to the customer.
Webhooks let you push real-time event data to an external URL (e.g., a Zapier zap, a CRM, or a custom system).
1. Go to **Settings → Webhooks**.
2. Click **+ New Webhook**.

3. Enter:
- **URL** — the destination endpoint
- **Events** — select which events to subscribe to (e.g., `work_order.completed`, `invoice.paid`)
- **Secret** — a shared secret for signature verification
4. Click **Save**. FieldForce Pro will send a `POST` request with JSON payload whenever a subscribed event occurs.
Add extra fields to entities (Work Orders, Contacts, Assets, etc.) to capture business-specific data.
1. Go to **Settings → Custom Fields**.
2. Select the entity type (e.g., `Work Order`).
3. Click **+ Add Field**.
4. Choose field type: `Text`, `Number`, `Date`, `Dropdown`, `Checkbox`, `File Upload`.
5. Enter a label and default value (optional).
6. Click **Save**. The field appears on all instances of that entity.
Customise the emails sent to customers for invoices, estimates, appointment reminders, etc.
1. Go to **Settings → Email Templates**.
2. Select a template (e.g., `Invoice Sent`, `Appointment Reminder`).
3. Edit the subject line and body using the rich-text editor.
4. Use template variables like `{{customer_name}}`, `{{invoice_total}}`, `{{appointment_date}}`.
5. Click **Save**. Changes apply to all future emails of that type.

user_questions: wf-est-convert-to-work-order — convert an approved estimate to a work order
exact_steps:
An approved estimate can be converted to a Work Order from two locations on the
Estimate Detail page: the **"Send to Customer"** collapse panel (`ApprovalTrackingView`)
and the main action bar (detail page header area, via `useConvertEstimateToWorkOrder`).
> Note: The backend also auto-converts the estimate to `converted_to_wo` after the
> customer signs via the magic link — this SOP covers the manual conversion path
> available to internal users.
---

- Estimate must have status `approved`.
- **"Convert to Work Order"** button is rendered only when `estimate.status === 'approved'`
inside the **"Send to Customer"** panel of `ApprovalTrackingView`.
- The **"Generate Invoice"** button (see **WF-EST-generate-invoice**) is also available
at this status in the detail page right column.
---
1. Click **"Estimates"** in the sidebar.

2. Locate the approved estimate — it appears in the **"All Estimates"** tab with a
green `Approved` tag.
3. Click the eye icon to navigate to `/estimates/:id`.

4. In the right column, expand the **"Send to Customer"** collapse panel (open by
default).
5. The panel shows a green "Customer Approved" or "Digitally Signed & Approved" banner.

6. Click **"Convert to Work Order"** ( icon, primary block button,
height 40 px, bold font weight).

7. The **"Convert to Work Order"** modal opens:
- **Title**: `"Convert to Work Order"`
- Alert: `"Convert estimate #<estimate_number> to a Work Order?"`
- Description: `"A new Work Order will be created. This action cannot be undone."`
- **OK button**: `"Convert"`

8. Click **"Convert"** to confirm.
Click `"Cancel"` to abort.

- A new Work Order is created and linked to the estimate.
- The estimate status transitions to `converted_to_wo` (purple tag, label
`"Converted To Wo"`).
- The **"Send to Customer"** panel now shows the "Converted to Work Order" state:
`"Successfully converted."`.
- The workflow stepper on the detail page advances to the final step **"Work Order"**.
- No further actions are available on the estimate (all transition buttons are hidden).

- User must be logged in and hold the `estimates:create` permission.
- User must be the **assigned estimator** OR an admin. If neither condition is met,
the application redirects to `/estimates` with the message:
`"Only the assigned estimator can create estimates"`.
- The **"Create Estimate"** button is only rendered when the **Drafts** tab is active
AND `canCreate` evaluates to `true`.
---
1. Click **"Estimates"** in the sidebar (calculator icon).
2. The Estimates list page opens. Click the **"Drafts"** tab.

3. Click the **"Create Estimate"** button (top-right, `+` icon). This navigates to
`/estimates/new`.

4. In the **"Client & Reference"** card, complete:
- **Customer / Contact** (required) — type to search and select from the dropdown.
- **Estimate Title** — e.g. `"HVAC Annual Maintenance Package"`.
- **Scheduled Date** — pick from the date picker (`"Select scheduled date"`).
- **Location** — search and select from `"Select service location"` dropdown; the
field is pre-populated when a linked SR supplies a location.

5. In the **"Estimate Details"** card (right column), complete:
- **Valid Until** (required) — select expiry date from `"Select expiry date"` date
picker. Past dates are disabled.
- **Priority** — optionally select: `Low`, `Medium`, `High`, or `Urgent`.
- **Estimate Date** is read-only (today's date, auto-set).

6. Add at least one line item (see **WF-EST-line-item-crud**).
The "Line Items" card border turns red and shows a **Required** tag until at least
one item is added.

7. Optionally fill in:
- **Notes** card — free text printed on the PDF.
- **Terms & Conditions** card — free text; click **"Use Default Terms"** to insert
the standard five-clause template.

8. Choose a save action (top-right button group):
- **"Cancel"** — navigates back to `/estimates` without saving.
- **"Save Draft"** — saves the estimate in `draft` status and
navigates back to `/estimates`.
- **"Save & Send for Review"** — saves the estimate, persists
all new line items, transitions status `draft → sent`, then navigates to `/estimates`.
If no line items have been added when either save button is clicked, an error toast
fires: `"Please add at least one line item before saving."` and the save is aborted.

- **Save Draft**: estimate is created with status `Draft` and appears in the **Drafts**
tab of the list page.
- **Save & Send for Review**: estimate is created and immediately sent for review;
status becomes `Sent` and the record appears on the **All Estimates** tab.

user_questions: wf-est-internal-review — internal reviewer approve or reject an estimate
exact_steps:
Internal review (multi-approver workflow) is managed from the **Approve / Reject** tab
on the Estimates list page. Each card in this tab represents one estimate assigned to
the current user for internal review. The component is `EstimateInternalReviewCard`.
---

- The current user is listed as an internal approver for the estimate (their approval
record has `status === 'PENDING'` and `approver_id === me.id`).
- The tab is named **"Approve / Reject"** (key `review`).
- Cards are only shown when at least one approval record exists for the estimate;
otherwise the card renders nothing.
---
1. Click **"Estimates"** in the sidebar.
2. Click the **"Approve / Reject"** tab.

3. Locate the estimate card showing your pending approval. The card header displays the
estimate number, status tag, total, and a progress badge `"<approved>/<total>"`.
4. If the card is collapsed, click the card header (toggles `"+ Expand"` / `"- Collapse"`).

5. Inside the card, find the approver step assigned to you. It is highlighted in blue
(border `rgba(22, 119, 255, 0.25)`, background `rgba(22, 119, 255, 0.08)`).
6. Click **"Approve"** .
7. The approval is processed immediately (no secondary confirmation dialog).

8. If this was the last pending approval, an alert appears:
`"All approvals completed — ready to send to customer."` with a **"Send Now"** button.
1–5. Same as Approve steps 1–5.
6. Click **"Reject"** .

7. The **"Reject Internal Review"** modal opens:
- **Title**: `"Reject Internal Review"`
- An alert: `"This will reject the internal approval and stop the approval chain."`
- **Comments (optional)** text area: placeholder `"Reason for rejection..."`
8. Optionally type a rejection reason.

9. Click **"Confirm Rejection"** (danger style OK button) to submit.
Click `"Cancel"` to discard.

When the last internal approval is confirmed, the card displays a success alert:
`"All approvals completed — ready to send to customer."` with a **"Send Now"**
(`SendOutlined`) button.
Clicking **"Send Now"** opens the **"Send Estimate to Customer"** modal at the page
level (see **WF-EST-send-to-customer**).
---

- **Approve**: the approver's step badge changes from a number to `"✓"`, and the
progress bar advances. If all approvers have approved/skipped, the estimate is
ready to send to the customer.
- **Reject**: the approver's step badge changes to `"✗"`, the progress bar turns red,
and an alert `"Internal review rejected"` is shown. The send workflow is blocked.

user_questions: wf-est-send-to-customer — send an estimate to the customer
exact_steps:
An estimate can be sent to the customer from two entry points:
(A) the **Send to Customer** panel on the Estimate Detail page (`ApprovalTrackingView`
component), and (B) the **"Send Estimate to Customer"** modal that opens automatically
after all internal approvals are completed on the **Approve / Reject** tab.
In both cases the same three delivery methods are available: WhatsApp, Email, and
Copy Sign Link.
---

- For **Entry Point A** (Detail page): estimate status must be one of `draft`, `sent`,
`viewed`, or `approved` AND either no internal approvals exist or all are completed
(`internalStage2Unlocked === true`).
- For **Entry Point B** (modal from Approve / Reject tab): triggered automatically
when the last internal approver clicks **"Approve"** or when **"Send Now"** is
clicked from the completion alert.
- If internal approvals exist and any are still `PENDING` or `REJECTED`, the
**Send to Customer** panel is locked and shows an alert; the send buttons are hidden.
---

user_questions: entry point a — from the estimate detail page
exact_steps: 1. Click **"Estimates"** in the sidebar.

2. Navigate to the target estimate by clicking the eye icon on any
tab row, reaching `/estimates/:id`.

3. In the right column, expand the **"Send to Customer"** collapse panel
(open by default).
4. Proceed to the **Delivery Method** steps below.

user_questions: entry point b — from the approve / reject tab (after internal review)
exact_steps: 1. Click **"Estimates"** in the sidebar.
2. Click the **"Approve / Reject"** tab.

3. After the last approval is processed, click **"Send Now"** in the success alert
(or the modal opens automatically). The **"Send Estimate to Customer"** modal appears.
4. Proceed to the **Delivery Method** steps below.

1. Click **"Send via WhatsApp"** ( icon, green button when phone is
present; disabled with tooltip `"No phone number on record for this customer"` /
`"No phone number on record"` when absent).
2. A magic sign link is generated.

3. The system opens `https://wa.me/<phone>?text=<pre-filled message>` in a new browser
tab. The message includes the estimate reference, total, expiry date, and the sign
link.
4. The modal closes (or `onClose` is called on the list-page modal).

1. Click **"Send via Email"** ( icon; disabled with tooltip
`"No email on record for this customer"` / `"No email on record"` when absent).

2. A magic sign link is generated and the **"Send Estimate via Email"** modal opens:
- **Title**: `"Send Estimate via Email"` .
- Alert: `"Magic link generated"` / `"Share this link with the customer. No login required."`
- A read-only **Sign Link** field displays the generated URL.
- A **"Copy Link"** button copies the link to
clipboard with toast `"Link copied"`.
- Footer button **"Open in Mail App"** opens the default
email client (`mailto:`) with pre-filled subject
`"Estimate <number> — Review & Sign"` and body containing the sign link.
- Footer button **"Close"** dismisses the modal.

1. Click **"Copy Sign Link"** .
- On the **list-page modal**: the link is generated, copied to clipboard, and the
modal closes. Toast: `"Link copied to clipboard"`.

`estimate.public_token` is set. Click to copy
`<origin>/estimate/sign/<public_token>` to clipboard.

Available only in the list-page modal (Entry Point B).

The customer receives (or the user holds) a magic link at the path
`/estimate/sign/<token>`. The customer can open this link without logging in,
review the estimate, and apply their digital signature. Upon signature, the backend
auto-transitions the estimate to `approved` and then `converted_to_wo`.

**Workflow:** Create a new maintenance plan
**Module:** Maintenance Plans
**Routes:** `/maintenance-plans` → `/maintenance-plans/new`
---

- The authenticated user must hold the permission `asset_maintenance_plans:create`.
The "Add Maintenance Plan" button is wrapped in
`<PermissionGuard permission="asset_maintenance_plans:create">` and is not rendered without this
permission.
- At least one asset must exist in the system; the Asset dropdown is populated from
`/assets?take=100`. If no assets exist, the dropdown is empty and the form cannot be submitted.
---

1. In the sidebar, click the navigation link that opens the **Maintenance Plans** page
(page title: "Maintenance Plans", subtitle: "Manage asset maintenance plans and schedules").

2. In the page header area, click the **Add Maintenance Plan** button .
The application navigates to `/maintenance-plans/new`.
The page title changes to **Add Maintenance Plan**,
subtitle: "Create a new maintenance plan".

3. The form is divided into two cards: **Plan Details** (left, 16-column width) and
**Schedule Settings** (right, 8-column width).
### Plan Details card

4. In the **Asset** dropdown , select the asset to link to this plan.
The dropdown supports search (`showSearch`, `optionFilterProp="children"`).
Each option displays the asset name followed by the serial number in parentheses
if a serial number exists, e.g. `Compressor Unit A (SN-12345)`.
Placeholder: `Select an asset`.
This field is required; leaving it empty shows the validation message
"Asset is required".
Note: The URL query parameter `asset_id` pre-selects an asset in this dropdown.
When navigating from an asset detail page with `?asset_id={id}`, the asset is
pre-filled automatically.

5. In the **Plan Name** field , type a name for the maintenance plan.
Placeholder: `e.g., Monthly HVAC Inspection`.
This field is required; leaving it empty shows "Plan name is required".

6. (Optional) In the **Description** field , enter a description of the
maintenance activities to be performed.
Placeholder: `Describe what maintenance activities should be performed...`.

7. In the **Frequency** dropdown , select one of the following options:
- `Daily`
- `Weekly`
- `Monthly` ← default initial value
- `Quarterly`
- `Yearly`
This field is required; leaving it empty shows "Frequency is required".
Side effect: When a frequency is selected and the **Next Due Date** field is currently
empty, the system automatically calculates and pre-fills the next due date as follows:
- Daily → today + 1 day
- Weekly → today + 1 week
- Monthly → today + 1 month
- Quarterly → today + 3 months
- Yearly → today + 1 year
### Schedule Settings card

8. (Optional) In the **Next Due Date** date picker , select the date on
which the maintenance is first due.
Format: `YYYY-MM-DD`. Placeholder: `Select next due date`.
If left blank the plan is saved without a scheduled date; the list shows "Not scheduled".
Note on create: the `last_completed_date` field is sent to the API only in Edit mode.
On create, the field is present in the UI but the value is discarded before the API call.

9. (Optional) In the **Last Completed Date** date picker , select
the most recent date the maintenance was completed.
Format: `YYYY-MM-DD`. Placeholder: `Select last completed date`.
Future dates are disabled (`disabledDate` blocks any date after today).
Note: This value is omitted from the create payload even if filled in here. It is only
persisted when editing an existing plan.

10. Toggle the **Auto Create Work Order** switch .
- Checked label: `Yes`; unchecked label: `No`.
- Initialises to `Yes` (enabled).
When enabled, the system will automatically create a work order when the plan becomes due.
The Schedule Preview area (read-only text below the switch) reflects this with:
"Work orders will be created automatically".

11. Toggle the **Active** switch .
- Checked label: `Active`; unchecked label: `Inactive`.
- Initialises to `Active` (enabled).
Note: On create, this value is also omitted from the API payload. It is only persisted
during edit.

12. Review the **Schedule Preview** panel (read-only, background `#f5f5f5`) in the Schedule
Settings card. It displays a live summary of frequency, next due date, and whether work
orders will be auto-created.

13. Click the **Create Plan** button .
- While the API call is in progress the button shows a loading spinner
.
- On success the application navigates back to `/maintenance-plans`.
- On failure the error is handled by the mutation hook.

14. To abort without saving, click the **Cancel** button at any time.
The application navigates back to `/maintenance-plans`.

- A draggable marker is placed.
